extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of analytical geometry and trigonometry (advanced undergraduates/graduate-level mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Deriving and presenting methods, formulas, and constructions in three-dimensional analytical geometry and elementary/advanced trigonometry (planes, normals, projections, areas, volumes, and trig identities); includes worked methods for integration of rational fractions and surveying problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer simple, recognised ultimate demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: "...it is incumbent upon all enquirers who adopt [general processes] to seek a more simple and recognised mode of ultimate demonstration..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using broad or novel methods to obtain general truths, also provide simpler/standard demonstrations as final justification. The author warns that reasoning from unelaborated conceptions is open to abuse and may introduce fallacious assumptions; hence one must ultimately reduce to a simple recognised proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize particular cases and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: "...exercise a careful scrutiny into the particular cases which arise from the variations in the hypothesis or the data respectively..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate special/exceptional parameter values and variations in hypotheses to discover peculiar conditions that may render a generally true theorem inapplicable or illusory in specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value symmetry and simplicity in constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes that some prior constructions (e.g., Poncelet's earlier constructions) "are wanting in the symmetry and simplicity which is peculiarly distinguishing the methods given above."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods and constructions that exhibit symmetry and simplicity; when presenting alternate constructions, comment on their relative symmetry and simplicity compared to existing approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior work and provide demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of earlier publications that gave constructions "without demonstration" and the statement of intent to publish demonstrations and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting constructions or claims that others have published without proof, provide full demonstrations and historical references; do not leave important steps undocumented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix conventions to avoid multi-valued ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Since any two of the coordinate planes make two angles (which are supplementary) with each other, ... this can only be avoided by laying down a conventional rule which shall restrict these symbols to one value each."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly adopt sign/magnitude conventions (e.g., for angles between planes) to remove ambiguity arising from multiple valid values (supplementary angles). State these conventions upfront and use them consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain sign consistency between directing cosines and coordinate projections
rubrics_metrics.description: "It will be observed that I here assume Qi, Q2, Q3 to have the same signs as Xi, the directing cosines of the normal to the plane Q, and hence if any one of these cosines, as /, be negative, the corresponding projection Qj must be taken negatively. This must be carefully kept in mind..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing coordinate projections and related quantities, ensure their algebraic signs correspond to the directing cosines of normals; carefully propagate sign choices through formulas to avoid sign errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain the plane equation via orthogonal projection; coefficients proportional to normal's length and directing cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: Method: let p be the length of the normal and \/ its directing cosines; the orthogonal projection of r on the normal is p and orthogonal projection of the broken line is xA+yB+zC, giving the equation to the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the orthogonal projection of position vectors onto the normal to derive the scalar equation of a plane. From that relation it follows that the absolute term and the coefficients of variables are proportional to the length and directing cosines of the normal (works for rectangular or oblique axes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive normals, projecting coefficients, and perpendicular line equations from plane coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Given plane A x + B y + C z = D, multiply and equate coefficients to obtain K and then the normal's length p and directing cosines; also derive equations of the normal and the straight line through a point perpendicular to the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the coefficient-equating procedure shown (multiply by 1/K etc.) to compute unknown normal parameters and to obtain equations for normals and perpendicular lines explicitly; present intermediate algebraic steps so results are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute angle between line and plane via complement and projection formula
rubrics_metrics.description: "The angle required [between line and plane] is the complement of that contained between the line and the normal to the plane... sin θ = (AS + BT + CU)/..." (formula (63) in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find the angle between a given straight line and a plane, compute the angle between the line and the plane's normal (via projecting coefficients/directing cosines) and take the complement; apply the explicit projection-based formula for sinθ as given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish perpendicularity and parallelism by cosine/dot-product conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for two planes to be perpendicular are obtained by setting the cosine (or the corresponding expression in coefficients) to zero; conditions for parallelism are equalities of the normals' directing cosines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the algebraic expressions for cosines between normals (derived from plane coefficients) to assert perpendicularity (cosine = 0) or parallelism (proportional normal coefficients). Provide the explicit expanded conditions when necessary to check edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation of plane through three points via linear system/determinantal expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the plane by q1 x + q2 y + q3 z = V and impose the three point constraints to solve the linear system; express q1,q2,q3,V in terms of determinants (equations (79)-(80)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing the equation of a plane through three given non-collinear points, set up and solve the 3×3 linear system for coefficients; provide determinant-form expressions for compactness and sign conventions for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute coordinate projections and relate plane area to projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate projections Qi, Q2, Q3 of a plane area Q relate via directing cosines X,Y,Z; Qi = Q * Xi etc., and an elegant relation for area in terms of projections is given (e.g., Q^2 = Qi'^2 + Q2'^2 + Q3'^2 - 2QiQ2 cos α3 - ... (eq.86)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute orthogonal projections on coordinate planes using directing cosines and preserve sign conventions. Use the provided formulae (Prop XVI-XVII) to compute area from its coordinate projections and include the geometric interpretation/assumptions (orientation of normals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume and determinant formula for tetrahedron
rubrics_metrics.description: Volume of a tetrahedron with vertices at origin and three points is given by a determinant-like expression (eq. 91): V = ±1/6 |det([x_i,y_i,z_i])| and special cases reduce to (1/6)XYZ for axes-aligned edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing a tetrahedron volume, use the scalar triple product/determinant formula; include sign considerations and the special-case simplifications when edges align with axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organized iterative method for resolving rational fractions in integration
rubrics_metrics.description: To integrate a rational function with repeated linear factors, organize successive divisions: expand numerators in powers of (x - a) up to required power, multiply coefficients by multipliers 1, m, m^2,... write rows, subtract successively, repeat n times to obtain numerators; reserve common denominator factors for the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform divisions in an ordered sequence determined by the factors' multiplicities, write down the denominators as headings, carry out repeated subtraction/division up to the necessary power only, and where convenient factor out and reserve common factors to simplify arithmetic; verify expansions by changing divisor order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange factors and denominators as headings; limit divisions to useful powers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Write down as a heading to each the denominators of the first quotient terms: which will exhibit the multipliers, the numbers of divisions to be made, and the proposed order of the processes... nothing beyond x^n in a process can be of use in any one which follows."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When executing the iterative division algorithm, lay out the denominators and multipliers clearly to guide the order and number of divisions; avoid carrying terms beyond the power that can affect subsequent steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend trig sum/difference formulas to all arc values via added/subtracted circumferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that sin and cos sum/difference formulas hold for any values of A and B by adding or subtracting whole circumferences (multiples of 2π or π) and using parity relations (equations (3)-(12)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extending identities to arcs outside [0,π/2], explicitly handle additions/subtractions of integer multiples of the circumference and use the parity properties of sine and cosine to translate to standard cases; document the parity/case analysis clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide simple geometric proofs for trig identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric derivation of sin(A+B) and cos(A+B) by constructing perpendiculars from points on the circle and using similar triangles to obtain OB·EC = BD·OF + BF·OD leading to sin(A+B)=sinA cosB + sinB cosA (eq.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer elementary geometric constructions and similarity arguments as proofs of trig sum/difference formulas; present the construction and link perpendicular lengths to sine/cosine components to make the identities transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve trigonometrical surveying problems by case-splitting and logarithmic reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: For problems like finding height from three stations or distances from angles subtended, reduce resulting algebraic relations to logarithmic equations and handle distinct cases depending on the relative sizes of the angles (produce different formula sets for each case (eqs. 19–24)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approaching surveying problems with multiple configurations, enumerate cases according to relative magnitudes of given angles, derive the appropriate algebraic/logarithmic equations for each case, and compute using logs/standard tables; explicitly show which formula applies in which configuration and include worked numerical examples.
